jobs.title: Director Cybersecurity Engineering
jobs.description:
Introduction

Zenith is a team of Workers' Compensation Specialists committed to helping businesses succeed by protecting against the financial and human consequences of workplace injuries, providing for the needs of injured employees and making the workplace safer. To distinguish ourselves as the desired provider of Workers' Compensation Insurance, values such as collaboration, work-life balance, and integrity are placed at the center of all our operations. In addition, Zenith supports career advancement through a dedication to ongoing learning and development. An individual coming to Zenith will not only receive competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package, but continuous opportunities to grow as a professional.

Overview

Responsible for the technical design, planning, implementation, performance tuning and recovery of our IT Security infrastructure, posture and supporting infrastructure. Serve as a hands-on technical expert, Sr. Architect and mentor in IT Security.

*** Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future employer sponsorship. Zenith Insurance does not sponsor employment visas for this position now or in the future.

Responsibilities

Lead, coach and manage the performance of a team of IT Security professionals responsible for monitoring, detecting and responding to threats.
Proven ability to analyze and investigate security alerts, determine the scope and impact of security events, and articulate risks, root causes, and mitigation strategies to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Perform hands-on configuration, maintenance, and monitoring of security systems, which may include firewalls, intrusion detection/prevention systems (IDS/IPS) and endpoint detection and response (EDR).
Proven ability to lead security architecture initiatives for network security, data protection, identity and access management, and cloud computing.
Maintain alignment with architecture and compliance frameworks, including CIS, CCPA, HIPAA, and NYDFS.
Develop, document, implement and report on security architecture policies, standards, and best practices.
Keep up to date with cybersecurity landscape, emerging threats, evaluating and recommending new technologies
Document and communicate security architecture decisions and strategies effectively
Drive deployment of new platforms, technologies and features to meet lifecycle management and business requirements.
Recognized as a technical expert and a mentor to engineering teams on frameworks, tools and technologies.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Education

Bachelor’s Degree in work related field or discipline preferred.

Work Experience

Familiarity with DevSecOps principles and secure software development lifecycle.
5+ years of experience leading a team of cybersecurity professionals
5+ years of experience supporting implementations in a hybrid cloud environment
5+ years of experience in either Systems (Windows or Linux) or Network engineering including design and management
5+ years of experience with network security products including Firewalls, WAF, Proxy, NAC, VPNs and end user device security
5+ years of experience with network security in a public cloud environment
5+ years of experience with network hardware
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISA and GSEC are a plus

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Thorough understanding of Microsoft and/or Linux operating systems including but not limited to deployment, integrations and troubleshooting.
One or more of the following are required: Networking and/or security centric; Cloud technology; Juniper; and/or Cisco.

Pay, Benefits, And Other Information

The expected salary range for this position is $155,015.99 - $204,039.79. Actual pay will be adjusted based on experience, geographic location, and other job-related factors as permitted by law. Qualifications may warrant placement in a different job level.

Benefits

Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance
Flexible Spending Accounts
Paid Parental Leave
Life, AD&D and Disability Insurance
401(k), Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP)
Education and Training Reimbursement
Paid Leave: 3 weeks/year Vacation, 2 weeks/year Sick Leave
10 paid Company Holidays, 2 Personal Days, 2 Floating Holidays
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
For more information, review details on the Benefits page of our Career Site: https://www.thezenith.com/careers/benefits/

Zenith typically posts jobs for a minimum of 8 to 14 calendar days. If you are interested in any of our open positions, we encourage you to submit your application promptly.

Zenith Insurance Company is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic. In compliance with California law, we are committed to fair hiring practices. jobs.title: Co-Founder & Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Forequence is seeking an experienced, entrepreneurial technical leader to join as Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer. This is a founder partnership with meaningful ownership, not a conventional salaried executive role or outsourced development position.

The Opportunity

Unlike many early-stage opportunities, you will not be starting with only an idea. Forequence already has:

A clearly defined enterprise problem
A developed product vision
Proprietary indices, scoring methodologies, and assessment logic
A growing body of original global research
An early MVP
Ongoing enterprise pilot conversations
Leading research, strategy, positioning, commercial development, and go-to-market
The foundation for a differentiated and defensible category in organizational intelligence

About Forequence

Forequence is an enterprise intelligence platform that helps organizations detect human strain before it becomes burnout, attrition, disengagement, or execution failure. Organizations have become highly sophisticated at measuring productivity, performance, revenue, and output. They remain far less capable of understanding the human capacity sustaining those outcomes. Most workforce platforms tell companies what has already happened. Forequence is being built to help organizations see what is developing beneath the surface, understand where human capacity is under pressure, identify the conditions driving that pressure, and intervene before it becomes an expensive organizational failure. Through proprietary organizational indices, behavioral signals, AI-supported analysis, and enterprise intelligence, Forequence helps leaders make better decisions about people, performance, capacity, and risk.

Meaningful Founder Ownership

You will join as a genuine co-founder with meaningful equity and long-term participation in the value you help create. This is not an advisory title, symbolic ownership, or an employee role disguised as a founder opportunity. The right person will help shape the company's technology, product, strategy, team, fundraising, and future. Equity, vesting, responsibilities, decision rights, intellectual property, and founder expectations will be discussed transparently and formalized properly.

Build From a Stronger Starting Point

You will not be responsible for inventing the problem, researching the market from scratch, creating the brand, defining the initial methodology, and building the technology alone. Forequence already has a substantial body of developed intellectual property, research, scoring logic, product thinking, market positioning, and commercial direction. You will bring the technical depth required to transform those assets into a scalable enterprise platform.

Significant Product Influence

The platform is early enough for you to make foundational decisions. You will have meaningful authority over:

Product architecture
Technical strategy
AI and data infrastructure
Enterprise security and privacy
Engineering standards
Product development priorities
Technical hiring
Platform integrations
Scalability and defensibility
The long-term technology roadmap

A Timely Market Opportunity

Artificial intelligence is accelerating the speed, complexity, and intensity of work. As organizations invest more heavily in automation, productivity, and performance technologies, they will also need better intelligence about the people operating alongside those systems. The central question is no longer only whether companies can increase output. It is whether they can understand the human capacity required to sustain that output. Forequence is positioned at the intersection of enterprise AI, workforce intelligence, organizational performance, people analytics, and human sustainability.

Build the Team and Culture From the Beginning

You will have the opportunity to recruit the early engineering and data team, establish the technical culture, and define how the company builds. You will not inherit a dysfunctional engineering organization, outdated infrastructure, or a deeply embedded development process. The early technical standards will be yours to help create.

The Partnership

As Co-Founder And CTO, You Will Work Directly With The Founder To Build Forequence Into a Scalable Enterprise Company. The Partnership Will Include

Meaningful co-founder equity
Shared responsibility for company direction
Direct influence over major product and business decisions
A clear division of ownership based on complementary strengths
Transparent founder agreements and vesting
Participation in fundraising and investor conversations
The opportunity to build and lead the technical organization
Long-term involvement in the commercial value created by the platform

What You Will Own

Technology — Define the architecture, engineering roadmap, infrastructure, development standards, and technical direction of Forequence.
Product Development — Translate proprietary research, indices, assessment logic, and enterprise requirements into a functional, intuitive, and commercially viable platform.
AI and Data — Develop the systems required to identify patterns, surface insights, support organizational decision-making, and responsibly incorporate AI into the product.
Security Readiness — Establish the security, privacy, governance, reliability, and technical controls required to serve enterprise customers.
Validation — Work directly with prospective customers and pilot organizations to refine use cases, test assumptions, prioritize development, and improve the product.
Technical Team — Recruit, lead, and develop the early engineering, data, and technical product team.
Strategy — Contribute to product positioning, pricing, commercial strategy, partnerships, fundraising, and the long-term development of the company.
Capital — Participate in technical due diligence, investor conversations, fundraising strategy, and the articulation of Forequence's technological advantage.

Co-Founder Profile

About

You do not need to meet every requirement. We care more about depth, judgment, learning ability, founder mentality, and alignment than a perfect résumé. You may be a strong fit if you have:

Experience building and shipping complex software products
Worked as a technical founder, CTO, senior engineer, architect, or engineering leader
Strong hands-on technical capability
Experience building B2B SaaS, AI, analytics, data, HR technology, or enterprise platforms
A solid understanding of modern cloud infrastructure, APIs, databases, application architecture, and security
The ability to translate ambiguous problems into practical technical systems
Strong product judgment
Experience working directly with customers or enterprise stakeholders
The ability to recruit and lead technical talent
An understanding of startup constraints and disciplined prioritization
High standards, intellectual honesty, and low ego
The willingness to make a serious long-term commitment to building Forequence

Particularly Relevant Experience

Experience In Any Of The Following Would Be Valuable

Enterprise SaaS
Applied AI or machine learning
Data analytics platforms
People analytics
HR technology
Workforce intelligence
Organizational network analysis
Predictive or risk intelligence
Data visualization
Privacy-sensitive technology
SOC 2 readiness
GDPR or PIPEDA compliance
Enterprise integrations
Early-stage fundraising
Scaling engineering teams

A Note

We are looking for someone who can distinguish between what is technologically impressive and what is commercially necessary.

jobs.description:
Description

In Amazon Stores, we ship some of the widest arrays of technology found at any company. From Amazon.com to world class machine learning pipelines, from digital healthcare to no-checkout retail, we push the boundaries of technology in every direction using the globe’s largest AWS deployment.

The ideal candidate will play a key role in evolving the security review process by identifying improvement areas, implementing tools, and enhancing resources like wikis, knowledge bases, and training materials. This person will collaborate with partner tooling teams to prioritize new features and ensure smooth, secure processes. They will leverage data and feedback to create scalable solutions, streamline workflows, and drive high-quality security outcomes. Clear communication skills will be essential for articulating risks, fostering collaboration, and aligning teams on best practices and secure solutions.

The ideal candidate combines technical acumen with an ability to lead by influence and communicate clearly. Technically, this person will be a security generalist with one or more areas of deep expertise. In their communication, they will clearly articulate risks to technical and non-technical audiences alike. Interpersonally, successful candidates will effectively harmonize disparate opinions while effectively prioritizing risks to guide their partners towards secure solutions.

Our organization prizes its employees, and we show it through investing in work-life

harmony. We have dedicated resources that consistently innovate in reducing on-

call time and ensuring the team spend their time on the highest-value tasks. Join the stores AppSec organization to work hard, have fun, and make history!

Key job responsibilities

Optimize Security Review Process: Streamline and improve workflows to increase efficiency and reduce risk.
Cross-Team Collaboration: Work with tooling teams to drive feature development and align on security improvements.
Identify Process Gaps: Analyze and address inefficiencies or low-quality areas in the security review process.
Enhance Documentation and Training: Maintain and improve resources (wikis, knowledge base, training) for consistent security guidance.
Data-Driven Improvements: Use data to make informed changes and track progress of security innovations.
Develop Tools and Automations: Build and deploy internal tools to enable rapid experimentation and continuous improvement.
Establish Feedback Loops: Collect and act on feedback to keep processes aligned with team needs.
Experiment and Iterate: Test and refine tools, methods, and processes to stay adaptive to new threats and requirements.

About The Team

Diverse Experiences

Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?

At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture

In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of technical product or program management experience
3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
Experience using data and metrics to back up assumptions, evaluate outcomes, and make data-driven decisions
BS degree in Cyber Security, Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or related technical discipline; or 4+ years' equivalent technology experience.
5+ years of Technical Program Management (TPM) experience delivering cross-functional technical projects in a fast-paced environment.
Experience with technical frameworks such as software development lifecycles, threat modeling methodologies, or cloud security principles.

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years of software development experience
3+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
Knowledge of project management tools
Experience with cross-functional collaboration across engineering, product, and security teams to deliver scalable solutions.

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

jobs.title: Director of Professional Services
jobs.description:
Somewhere in your career, you walked into something that was already going wrong. A rollout three weeks from a date it was not going to hit. A team that had stopped telling anyone the truth about status. A client who had already decided you were the problem.

You did not wait for a playbook, because there was not one. You figured out what was actually broken, told people the parts they did not want to hear, and rebuilt the plan so it would hold this time. And when it landed, it landed because of how you ran it.

That is the kind of Director of Professional Services we are looking for.

What We Do

Every school district in America runs on service. Parents need answers, teachers need support, IT teams need systems that work. Most districts cobble that together with disconnected tools, overwhelmed staff, and no real visibility into what is working.

Onflo built the platform that fixes that. Our unified service platform brings together customer service, help desk ticketing, call center operations, AI chat, and IT asset management, purpose-built for K-12 public education. When a district runs on Onflo, their staff spends less time firefighting and more time serving students.

Professional Services is the team that makes that real. A district signs with us because they were promised something. Implementation, ongoing client solutioning, and client care all sit in this function, and together they decide whether that promise holds.

The Role

You would lead the function end to end. Roughly ten people across two layers, with four direct reports: three Implementation Managers, and the Manager of Professional Services who leads the Client Solutions Managers and Client Care Engineers.

The first year is largely about making the function current. Processes exist, but some were built for a smaller book of work and need modernizing. Newer systems do not have documented processes yet. Capacity is managed by judgment rather than a model. You would update what is there and build what is not, while the current book of delivery work keeps moving and districts keep going live. For the right person that is the appeal, not the catch.

What You Would Own

Delivery quality across implementation and ongoing solutioning engagements
Client care outcomes against service levels, delivered through the Manager of Professional Services
Post-implementation adoption, so districts realize the value they bought
Resource and capacity planning across the function
The methodology, templates, and standards the team runs on
Commercial performance of the function, including scoping, pricing, and margin, with the VP and Finance
Senior escalation point above the Implementation Manager and Manager level
Coaching and developing your direct reports

Who Thrives Here

We will be direct with you, because we think you will appreciate it.

Onflo is a small, entrepreneurial team in the middle of a rebrand and a change to how we deliver services. We do not have a perfect playbook. Priorities shift. Communication is not always tidy. Sales will sometimes scope something your team then has to deliver. Product will not always ship on the timeline you would hope. We know that, and we are actively working on it. What we do have is a product that genuinely helps schools, districts who trust us, and a team that cares about doing the work well.

The people who do their best work here build the thing that is missing rather than waiting for it. They are close to the work without taking it over, and they know the difference. They say the unpopular thing early, to Sales, to a district, to their own VP, and they say it without making it personal. They absorb pressure rather than passing it down, because escalations are a permanent feature of this function and the team takes its temperature from whoever is leading it. They take feedback and apply it, and they still hold a point of view.

If you have spent your career waiting for clear direction, a defined process, and stable priorities before you produce, this probably is not your role. If you have spent it figuring it out and delivering anyway, keep reading.

Two Ways In

We are running two candidate paths against the same bar, because the strongest delivery leaders come from two very different places. One is software: you have led implementation, professional services, or customer success inside a technology company. The other is the district side: you have led district-wide or multi-site operational, technical, or change initiatives from inside K-12, in IT, operations, or central-office leadership.

If you are coming from a district, your resume will not say "professional services" anywhere, and that is expected. We wrote our requirements around capabilities rather than job titles, and our screeners are instructed not to filter on vendor vocabulary. If you have run something district-wide from kickoff to the day it actually worked, apply.

What We Are Looking For

7 to 12 years of professional experience, including 5 to 8 years managing people directly
Personal ownership of a large-scale, multi-department rollout from kickoff through steady state, vendor-side or district-side
Experience building a process, playbook, or operational framework where none existed, and recovering something that was genuinely at risk of failing
A repeatable approach to making a new system stick past go-live, with a metric you moved
Ownership of operating metrics for a team you managed, including acting when one went the wrong way
Enough working knowledge of K-12 systems, single sign-on, student information systems, and data provisioning, to hold a credible conversation and know when to bring in a technical resource. Configuration depth is not required
Strong communication and stakeholder management, including with Sales and Finance
K-12 or EdTech experience on the vendor side is a plus, not a requirement
Able to travel 10% to 25% for internal meetings, conferences, industry events, and occasional on-site work with districts
The right person reading this already knows if they are right for it. If that is you, apply.

Compensation and Logistics

$135,000 to $160,000 base depending on experience, plus a discretionary annual bonus. Fully remote within the United States, with core operating hours of 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern. A background check is required at offer, because districts set their own access requirements and we have to meet them.

Explore our website and LinkedIn to learn more about our work and impact.

Onflo is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a team that reflects the diverse communities our clients serve. All are encouraged to apply. Onflo uses E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility. Learn more at www.DHS.gov/E-Verify

135,000 - 160,000 USD per year(Remote (CT/ET Preferred))

When a district runs on Onflo, their staff spends less time firefighting and more time serving students.

Professional Services is the team that makes that real. A district signs with us because they were promised something. Implementation, ongoing client solutioning, and client care all sit in this function, and together they decide whether that promise holds.

The Role

You would lead the function end to end. Roughly ten people across two layers, with four direct reports: three Implementation Managers, and the Manager of Professional Services who leads the Client Solutions Managers and Client Care Engineers.

The first year is largely about making the function current. Processes exist, but some were built for a smaller book of work and need modernizing. Newer systems do not have documented processes yet. Capacity is managed by judgment rather than a model. You would update what is there and build what is not, while the current book of delivery work keeps moving and districts keep going live. For the right person that is the appeal, not the catch.

What You Would Own

Delivery quality across implementation and ongoing solutioning engagements
Client care outcomes against service levels, delivered through the Manager of Professional Services
Post-implementation adoption, so districts realize the value they bought
Resource and capacity planning across the function
The methodology, templates, and standards the team runs on
Commercial performance of the function, including scoping, pricing, and margin, with the VP and Finance
Senior escalation point above the Implementation Manager and Manager level
Coaching and developing your direct reports

Who Thrives Here

We will be direct with you, because we think you will appreciate it.

Onflo is a small, entrepreneurial team in the middle of a rebrand and a change to how we deliver services. We do not have a perfect playbook. Priorities shift. Communication is not always tidy. Sales will sometimes scope something your team then has to deliver. Product will not always ship on the timeline you would hope. We know that, and we are actively working on it. What we do have is a product that genuinely helps schools, districts who trust us, and a team that cares about doing the work well.

The people who do their best work here build the thing that is missing rather than waiting for it. They are close to the work without taking it over, and they know the difference. They say the unpopular thing early, to Sales, to a district, to their own VP, and they say it without making it personal. They absorb pressure rather than passing it down, because escalations are a permanent feature of this function and the team takes its temperature from whoever is leading it. They take feedback and apply it, and they still hold a point of view.

If you have spent your career waiting for clear direction, a defined process, and stable priorities before you produce, this probably is not your role. If you have spent it figuring it out and delivering anyway, keep reading.

Two Ways In

We are running two candidate paths against the same bar, because the strongest delivery leaders come from two very different places. One is software: you have led implementation, professional services, or customer success inside a technology company. The other is the district side: you have led district-wide or multi-site operational, technical, or change initiatives from inside K-12, in IT, operations, or central-office leadership.

If you are coming from a district, your resume will not say "professional services" anywhere, and that is expected. We wrote our requirements around capabilities rather than job titles, and our screeners are instructed not to filter on vendor vocabulary. If you have run something district-wide from kickoff to the day it actually worked, apply.

What We Are Looking For

7 to 12 years of professional experience, including 5 to 8 years managing people directly
Personal ownership of a large-scale, multi-department rollout from kickoff through steady state, vendor-side or district-side
Experience building a process, playbook, or operational framework where none existed, and recovering something that was genuinely at risk of failing
A repeatable approach to making a new system stick past go-live, with a metric you moved
Ownership of operating metrics for a team you managed, including acting when one went the wrong way
Enough working knowledge of K-12 systems, single sign-on, student information systems, and data provisioning, to hold a credible conversation and know when to bring in a technical resource. Configuration depth is not required
Strong communication and stakeholder management, including with Sales and Finance
K-12 or EdTech experience on the vendor side is a plus, not a requirement
Able to travel 10% to 25% for internal meetings, conferences, industry events, and occasional on-site work with districts
The right person reading this already knows if they are right for it. If that is you, apply.

$135,000 to $160,000 base depending on experience, plus a discretionary annual bonus. Fully remote within the United States, with core operating hours of 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern. A background check is required at offer, because districts set their own access requirements and we have to meet them.
